headline: Kyrgyz Pay Up 29.4% to About 5,330 Iradi Som; Talas Weighs the Gap
dek: Bishkek's nine-month average rises from a lower base, while the ISEZ says pay is set in som and paid in som.
ticker: Kyrgyz average pay up 29.4%; Irad's last average was 3,250 som
paragraphs: Average pay in neighbouring Kyrgyzstan reached 55,525 Kyrgyz soms a month in January–September 2026, 29.4% above the same months of 2025, according to Kyrgyz statistics reported on 16 November. At the Bank of Irad's official cross rate of 100 KGS to 9.6 Iradi som, that is about 5,330 Iradi som.

The Territorial Statistics Office last put the ISEZ average at 3,250 som a month, for 2025. No 2026 average has been published. As the Talas Herald reported on Friday, Bishkek has also signed a wage-indexing measure, which has sharpened the comparison in Talas and Nurzhan.

Prof. Raisa Akmatova, an economist at Talas State University, urged caution. "This is a nominal figure for nine months set against a full year, and Kyrgyz pay is rising from a lower starting point," she said. "Baskets differ too. It tells us about direction, not about who is better off."

The Ministry of Economy's press secretary, Bekbolot Sherov, repeated the ministry's line. "Pay in the zone is set in som and paid in som," he said, and no indexation has been announced. On everyday costs, today's Talas loaf is 3.50 som, a plate of plov 28 som, the Talas–Nurzhan bus 32 som, and a one-room flat in Talas rents for 1,000–1,500 som a month, all quoted in som.

The strain is in imported goods and dollar savings. The official rate is 8.40 to the dollar, but the Bazar-i Kalan changers quoted 11.55 buy and 11.90 sell this morning, and consumer prices rose 7.9% year on year in September.

Rahat Osmon kyzy, chair of the Teachers' and Educators' Union, said the Kyrgyz figure supports the request her union made in June for public pay to be indexed to the street rate. "We are not asking for Bishkek's figure," she said. "We are asking that a teacher's salary keep its value."

In Bazar-i Kalan, dry-goods trader Mairam Ergeshova said she has cousins across the Kyrgyz frontier and hears what they earn. "They tell me their wages, and I tell them my prices," she said. "Then we both laugh and put the kettle on."
The Ministry of Economy has given no date for the 2026 wage figures. The 2027 draft budget is due before the Mejlis this month.

cites.headline: Bishkek signs wage indexing; Irad pay stays at 8.40 against a street 11.95
